open_points.subject: random identifiers for entity records
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation and collision retry for records created by `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects`?
options: A shared lower-level identifier module mints them
Each record-owning module implements its own random-ID generation and collision retry
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and uniqueness-check every random identifier inside the record-creation transaction.

open_points.subject: file-content digests
open_points.text: Every content-derived identity and digest in this kernel is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the model's meaning facts — never of who created it or when. / The body is described ... as ... the SHA-256 of its content. / `content_digest`, `size_bytes`.
open_points.question: Are file digests SHA-256 of the raw file bytes or of a canonical-JSON representation, and which module owns the shared digest operation used by trial outputs, spooled files, fixtures and multipart request descriptions?
options: SHA-256 of raw file bytes, owned by `canonical_values`
SHA-256 of raw file bytes, computed independently by each producing module
SHA-256 of a specified canonical-JSON representation, owned by `canonical_values`
open_points.default_guess: Use lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the raw file bytes and make `canonical_values` own a shared byte-digest capability.
